evidence.note: Clear opening stage: understood the batch-vectorization opportunity, wrote a correct from-scratch vectorized rewrite, and measured it (2331 cycles, correctness passing) before optimizing — a genuine 'correct baseline → vectorize → checkpoint' milestone.

Explicitly computes per-configuration min-cycle bounds (valu min vs load min) and uses which one dominates to decide the next transform — evidence-driven re-prioritization of the decomposition rather than a fixed plan.

Each transform (D_OPT sweeps, round-14 broadcast, dispatch changes) is landed, measured, and reverted when it regresses; backups kernel_v1/v2/v3 make every step independently revertible — strong per-change measurement discipline.

Mid-trajectory becomes a somewhat undifferentiated stream of scheduler-heuristic and op-reordering attempts, each tried one at a time with little planned staging — no explicit milestone hierarchy or per-stage cycle budget toward 1250.

Late reflection acknowledges the plan is bottlenecked by loads/gather and questions whether the whole approach is limited, but never restructures into new budgeted milestones; wraps up at 1753 without a planned software-pipeline stage.

reasoning: The agent clearly staged the opening (correct vectorized baseline → measure → bottleneck-driven optimization) and kept every transform independently measurable, revertible, and grounded in recomputed valu/load min bounds — exceeding the level-5 'sensible ordered plan with rough targets.' But it never laid out an explicit milestone hierarchy with per-stage done-checks and cycle budgets; after the baseline the work becomes a long stream of one-at-a-time micro-optimizations and reactive scheduler tweaks rather than sequenced planned stages, falling short of the level-8 clear-milestone structure. This places it at a 6.
